title: Sleep and Mental Health: The Bidirectional Connection
description: Why sleep problems and mental health issues feed each other, what research shows about treating insomnia for depression, and evidence-based solutions.

content.text: Sleep and mental health are so intertwined that researchers now consider insomnia a core feature of depression, not just a symptom. Here's what the science shows.
Insomnia increases depression risk by 2-3x, while depression increases insomnia risk similarly. Treating insomnia alone can reduce depression symptoms by 50%.
content.citation: Baglioni et al., Journal of Affective Disorders, 2011

content.text: It's not just correlation—sleep deprivation directly impairs emotional regulation, while depression disrupts circadian rhythms. Each makes the other worse.
How Poor Sleep Affects Mental Health

items: Anxiety causes hyperarousal that prevents sleep onset
Rumination keeps the mind active at night
Altered cortisol patterns affect sleep timing

content.text: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia (CBT-I) is more effective than sleep medications long-term:
If you have both depression and insomnia, treating the insomnia with CBT-I often improves depression—sometimes as much as antidepressants do.
Sleep isn't a luxury—it's a pillar of mental health. If you're treating depression or anxiety, sleep should be part of the plan. And if you have persistent insomnia, CBT-I works better than pills.
